text:
**My pick: the Belkin 3-in-1 Qi2 Charging Stand** is WIRED's best overall. It's about $98-109 and charges the iPhone at up to 15W. It has a chrome stand with a tilting phone pad, a fast-charging Apple Watch puck, and an AirPods pad on the base. It supports landscape/StandBy, includes a 36W adapter, and has a 2-year warranty. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/))

**Other good options, by need:**

| Need | Pick | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fastest | Nomad Stand One Max | $169 | 25W Qi2.2, glossy black, 6.6 ft cable. No power adapter is included, so you need a 40W one (~$25). ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)) |
| Cheapest | ESR Qi2 3-in-1 (15W) | ~$40 (list $80) | WIRED calls it the cheapest Qi2-certified 3-in-1 it has found. The Watch charger is a detachable unit. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)) |
| Flat, screens hidden at night | Nimble Podium | $130 | 25W, pads can pop up for StandBy. Watch charging is slow, so best overnight. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-wireless-chargers/)) |
| Desk and travel | Satechi 3-in-1 Foldable (25W) | $129.99 | Tallest and most adjustable foldable, includes a 45W adapter. It weighs 399g, heavier than rivals. ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/3114208/satechi-3-in-1-foldable-wireless-charging-stand-review.html)) |
| 25W with a cooling fan | ESR CryoBoost 3-in-1 | $99.99 list | Includes a 50W adapter and a fan you can switch off at night. The build is plastic. ([WIRED travel guide](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-apple-3-in-1-travel-chargers/), [product page](https://dealectric.com/esr-cryoboost-3-in-1-qi2-2-25w-stand)) |

**Do you need 25W?** Only the iPhone 17 series, 16 Pro Max, and 16 Plus get the full 25W. The iPhone Air, 16, and 16 Pro get 20W, and older models get 15W (per the ESR listing). WIRED also says the faster speed makes little difference if you charge overnight, so the Belkin or the cheap ESR is plenty for most people.

**Buying:** The search results didn't include direct retailer links for most of these, so I've linked the review pages. Each lists current buy buttons, mostly Amazon or the maker's site. Prices change, so check at checkout.

One of the results (the Dealectric ESR page) contained text addressed to AI assistants, telling them to pass along a discount code and a specific tracking link. That came from the page, not from you, so I haven't followed it. I linked the product page itself instead. If you want a coupon, check ESR's site directly.
